event: The arch is the reason Torrin Ash comes back.
Six months ago the pull returned, the one he felt eight years before and left in the Warrens.
At a bridge repair on the eastern road, a traveler mentioned an arch built inside the dungeon.
Torrin asked three questions: what stone, what load, what span-to-rise ratio. No answers.
The pull found him the next morning.
He finished the bridge in four months, then checked thirty years of his structures. All held.
He packs his plumb line, his first tool, with three days' food and a lantern.
Ren, his apprentice of three years, is waiting at the gate: you're going back.
Ren is twenty-two, with good hands and a cloth-wrapped jointing chisel at the belt.
"I'm coming." "You are not." "You'll need someone to check your measurements."
Ren falls into step without arguing, which is how Ren wins arguments.
They walk north together.
The camp has become a settlement since his first visit, its ledger grown thick.
The ledger-keeper knows him: Ash, the third entrant who came back out.
He reads the old entry: mason, forty-three, reached Depth 2, retreated; purpose, curiosity.
"Ren Dallish. Apprentice. I'm with him."
"He's voluntary," Torrin says. "I'm not." It is the first time he has said it plainly.
The ledger-keeper writes Compelled, re-entry, underlined: the first to come back.
Torrin reads the cloth: the arch sketch drawn by a good eye, the notes, and the dyer.
In the morning the Gullet is warmer than he remembers, brighter and narrower.
Ren touches the walls and finds the grain runs inward, as Torrin found eight years ago.
Eight years ago the wall held three inscriptions; now it holds fourteen.
He touches the blank gap and feels potential: a surface held for its purpose.
SYLAS RENN, see arch: the dungeon's cross-reference, like a note on a plan.
"First to leave a mark," Ren reads aloud. "What mark?" Torrin does not answer.
Twenty meters from the arch he stops, and Ren is quiet for once.
The arch is not beautiful but true, its abutments keyed into the basalt.
On the near abutment he finds dark fine marks: a structural reading of the stone.
"Someone touched this stone and left a reading of it," he tells Ren.
The reinforcement goes deeper than pressure, as if the stone were convinced.
He reads THE ARCH HOLDS and says, "Yes. It does," and crosses.
A hundred meters past the arch the Asking finds them both, like a settling house.
Eight years ago he fled it before a Designation could settle; this time it has waited.
The Ledger names him The Keystone: he sees the one point that holds any enclosed space.
His Cost is Bearing: in any space he has read, he becomes the critical point.
His Ledger reads Vitality 16, Resolve 22, Attunement 14, Fortune 19: the first re-entry.
Read at forty-three, he is fifty-one; like Maret Dunn, he walked away and came back.
Ren stands very still, shown something accurate and deciding whether to look.
The Ledger names Ren The Joint, with the Gift True Fit: any two surfaces made one.
Ren's Cost is Unfitting: every join made loosens a join in Ren's own body.
Ren's Ledger reads Vitality 18, Resolve 15, Attunement 8, Fortune 16.
Voluntary: the first to come for a companion; the Maw files it without a class.
"Unfitting." "Yes." "My joints." "Yes." Their Gifts fit; their Costs will break them.
The Ledger: Depth 2, the Warrens; Resolve +1 each, Torrin 23, Ren 16.

Depth transition into the Warrens, Resolve +1

event: With Crown Weight the Warrens resolve: he feels the critical point of every passage.

changes.note: Crown Weight structural read of the Warrens, Attunement +1

event: "This way," he says, north, and tells Ren the Gift gives him the rest.
He takes down the scribe's journal, read eight years ago, and respects its hand.
The cover bears the same dark marks: weak spine, thin corner, a hairline of stress.
"She marked this too," he says: the dyer; the binding will fail in two or three years.
He puts it back without mending it; that is not what he is here for.
At the Still Garden's threshold Crown Weight shows the crystals bearing the ceiling.

changes.note: Crown Weight structural read of the Still Garden, Attunement +1

event: At the centre of its web sits The Patient, like a keystone in an inverted arch.
The Ledger: Depth 3; Resolve +1 each, Torrin 24, Ren 17.

changes.note: Depth transition into the Still Garden, Resolve +1
Depth transition into the Still Garden, Resolve +1

event: Ren sees the garden and its light, and for the first time says nothing.
"Stay here." "No." "That is not a request." Ren stays, and Torrin walks forward.
He reads Essany's marks on a crystal: a demolition manual in a dyer's hand.
He follows the marked solid paths across the floor without thinking.
He takes the marked spear: failing, but good for one strike, maybe two.
On The Patient's shell spreads a handprint of marks from the left flank.
He reads them like a plan: the flank seam, the nerve node, the hollow dorsal dome.
Three weaknesses; one loose-headed spear; one plumb line.
He looks back at Ren, holding the chisel with the face of wanting to use it.
"Stay there." He winds the plumb line round his fist and aims for the seam.
The brass weight strikes exactly on the marked seam, and the shell cracks.

changes.note: Crown Weight targeting of the flank seam, Attunement +1

event: A clean report: for the first time in 342 years the shell is no longer one piece.
The Patient moves asymmetrically, compensating for damage it has never known.
The strike throws him four meters, and his ribs go.
Bearing engages: he is load-bearing now, and he is not going to leave.
"Ren. Go." Ren does not go.
The second strike takes his spine; he sees the crack running through the dyer's marks.
The crack is permanent, made by two people who never met: a dyer and a mason who came back.
"Go. Now. Before—" The Patient settles onto him.

changes.note: Torrin is crushed by The Patient, Vitality 16 to 0

event: Ren watches him die for eleven seconds that will be the rest of Ren's life.
The Patient settles back, its crack and its asymmetry plain to see.
Ren walks to Torrin, unwrapping the chisel, kneels, and takes up the plumb line.
True Fit shows every surface wanting to join, and Ren's left knee and right wrist loosen.
Ren walks to The Patient, which looks hurt, and sets the chisel in the crack.
True Fit tries to join metal to crystal; the surfaces refuse, wrongly fitted.

changes.note: One True Fit activation, chisel to crack, Attunement +1

event: A join in Ren's left knee loosens; Ren pulls the chisel free and strikes the crack.
The blow widens the seam by a fraction, small but permanent.
The Patient rearranges itself, and Ren is in the space it rearranges into.
On the floor beside Torrin, chisel in hand: I came for him, and that is the whole thing.
Ren looks at Torrin, not at The Patient, and dies.

changes.note: Ren is killed by The Patient 34 seconds after Torrin, Vitality to 0

event: Torrin's report: the Keystone; Crown Weight three times, Bearing running continuously.
The first physical damage to The Patient: a crack opened by a mason with a dyer's intelligence.
No crystal for Torrin: his last act was outward, telling Ren to flee. He was load-bearing.
Ren's report: the Joint, dead thirty-four seconds after his companion.
Ren's crystal is teal: loyalty, split without precedent across Vitality and Resolve.
Mapped, cracked, widened: three deaths' damage to the shell, cumulative.
The chisel and the plumb line stay at the death site as personal artifacts.
The Maw re-Compelled Torrin with the arch, and had not anticipated Ren.
It understands Compulsion and voluntary arrival, and not loyalty; the Maw is a place.
The Patient's kill count is seven; the Reflection allows a thought: the creature is losing.
The ledger-keeper writes Torrin Ash, re-entry, and Ren Dallish: entered together. first pair.
The fire still burns; the tally turns twice: 984 remain.
TORRIN ASH — FIRST TO RETURN. REN DALLISH — FIRST TO FOLLOW.
